title: Record, watch, fix one thing
speaker: Sam Example
aiTool: an image model, from a written prompt
intro: Everything from the talk, one section per slide, so you can listen instead of taking notes. The one thing to do this week is at the end.

body: You cannot hear yourself while you speak: your attention is on the next sentence. A recording hears everything, and you already carry the camera that makes one.
Put the phone where the back row would sit, at eye height, and press record. That is the whole kit.
A recording shows you twenty things at once. Pick one, the one that costs the room most, and fix only that before the next talk.
Write it down as something you can count: "fewer than two fillers a minute", not "sound more confident". The next recording tells you whether you made it.
The first run is for comfort: get through it end to end and note where you stall. The second is for the weak spots the first one showed. The third is polish: lock the first minute and the last lines.
Record and watch each one. Three is enough to hear the difference between the first and the last.

You do not need tools to rehearse, but they turn impressions into numbers. This command keeps only the sound of a recording, ready for a speech-to-text tool such as Whisper, which gives you every word with its timestamp.
From that transcript, count your words per minute and your filler words. Conversational pace is about 130 to 160 words a minute.

sections.concept: The question that makes it yours
body: Here the screen went black and you were asked which habit you would fix first. The answer is your goal from slide 2.
Most people name a filler word or speed. Both are easy to count in a recording, which is why they make good first goals.
The last slide pointed here, so nobody had to take notes. Your one next step is just below.

nextStep.action: Record one run-through of your next talk this week and watch it back once.
nextStep.why: One recording shows you more than ten silent read-throughs of your notes.
how: Prop your phone at eye height, in landscape, about where the back row would sit.
Give the whole talk once without stopping, as if the room were full.
Watch it back the same day at normal speed, with a pen.
Write down the one habit you would fix first, as something you can count.
Record again before the talk and count only that.
